sections.readable_text: What is the sum of the solutions of the equation [MATH: x(x - 3) - 14 = 3x(x - 6)?]

sections.normalized_html:
The standard form of a quadratic equation is [MATH: ax^2 + bx + c = 0,\qquad a \neq 0.]

First, by expanding the products on both the left-hand side and the right-hand side and then simplifying, we get [MATH: x(x − 3) − 14|= 3x(x − 6); x^{2} − 3x − 14|= 3x^{2} − 18x.]

Rewriting the above equation as a quadratic equation in standard form, we obtain [MATH: x^{2} − 3x − 14|= 3x^{2} − 18x; − 2x^{2} + 15x − 14|= 0.]

For the last equation, we have [MATH: a=-2,] [MATH: b=15,] and [MATH: c=-14.]

Now, recall that [MATH: -\dfrac{b}{a}] gives the value of the sum of the solutions to the quadratic equation. Therefore, [MATH: -\dfrac{b}{a} = -\dfrac{15}{(-2)} = \dfrac{15}{2}.]

Therefore, the sum of the solutions to our original equation is [MATH: \dfrac{15}{2}.]
